title.en: From Search to Answers: Build a Local RAG Pipeline with all-MiniLM-L6-v2

description.en: Level up from semantic search to a full retrieval-augmented generation pipeline: chunk your documents, index them with all-MiniLM-L6-v2's 384-dim embeddings, retrieve the best evidence, and assemble a grounded prompt â€” all on a laptop CPU.

story_variants.en:
## The Open-Book Exam

Vaathiyaar slides a thick textbook across the desk. "A language model answering from memory is a student in a *closed-book* exam â€” confident, sometimes wrong, and it can't cite a page. **RAG** â€” Retrieval-Augmented Generation â€” turns it into an *open-book* exam. Before answering, we fetch the exact paragraphs that matter and hand them to the model. The librarian doing that fetching? Our old friend `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`."

You already know how to encode sentences and rank them by cosine similarity. Today we assemble those pieces into the four-stage pipeline that powers real assistants â€” including Homie's fully local index.

### The Four Stages of RAG

| Stage | What happens | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Chunk | Split documents into retrieval-sized pieces | plain Python |
| 2. Index | Encode every chunk once into 384-dim vectors | all-MiniLM-L6-v2 |
| 3. Retrieve | Encode the query, rank chunks by cosine similarity | `util.semantic_search` |
| 4. Augment | Paste top chunks into the prompt as evidence | f-string |

Only stage 2 costs real compute, and you pay it **once**. Every question afterwards is a cheap encode-and-compare.

### Why Chunking Matters

Embedding a whole document blurs its meaning into one average vector â€” a page about both refunds and shipping matches neither query well. Chunks of roughly 2-5 sentences keep each vector *about one thing*, so retrieval stays sharp:

```python
def chunk(text: str, size: int = 3) -> list[str]:
    sentences = [s.strip() for s in text.split(".") if s.strip()]
    return [". ".join(sentences[i:i+size]) + "."
            for i in range(0, len(sentences), size)]
```

### Retrieval: The Heart of the Pipeline

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer, util

model = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
chunk_emb = model.encode(chunks, convert_to_tensor=True)  # index once

hits = util.semantic_search(
    model.encode("How do I get my money back?", convert_to_tensor=True),
    chunk_emb, top_k=3
)[0]
evidence = [chunks[h["corpus_id"]] for h in hits]
```

No keyword overlap needed â€” "money back" lands on the *refund policy* chunk because the vectors share meaning.

### Augment: Ground the Model

```python
prompt = f"""Answer using ONLY the context below.
If the context is insufficient, say so.

Context:
{chr(10).join(evidence)}

Question: {question}"""
```

Feed this to any LLM â€” a local Ollama model, Qwen3-0.6B, or an API â€” and the answer is grounded in *your* documents instead of the model's fuzzy memory. Swap the corpus and the same pipeline answers questions about legal contracts, lecture notes, or your codebase.

### Why MiniLM Is the Right Retriever Here

At ~90 MB and 384 dimensions, `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` encodes hundreds of chunks per second on CPU. Your retrieval layer stays fast, private, and free â€” the expensive LLM only ever sees the handful of chunks that matter.

> **Key Insight:** RAG is just semantic search with a purpose: **chunk once, index once, retrieve per question, augment the prompt.** The quality of the final answer is decided before the LLM even runs â€” by how well your chunks isolate single ideas and how well your retriever ranks them. Master retrieval and the generation step becomes the easy part.

    """Return the k chunks most semantically similar to the query, best first."""

    # 2. Encode the query into the same vector space
    # 3. Use util.semantic_search(query_emb, chunk_emb, top_k=k)
    # 4. Map each hit's 'corpus_id' back to its chunk text

chunks = [
    "Refunds are issued within 14 days of purchase.",

Each hit is a dict with 'corpus_id' (index into chunks) and 'score'
Hits are already sorted best-first, so just map them: [chunks[h['corpus_id']] for h in hits]

from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer, util

_model = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

def retrieve_top_k(query, chunks, k=2):
    chunk_emb = _model.encode(chunks, convert_to_tensor=True)
    q_emb = _model.encode(query, convert_to_tensor=True)
    hits = util.semantic_search(q_emb, chunk_emb, top_k=k)[0]
    return [chunks[h["corpus_id"]] for h in hits]

chunks = [
    "Refunds are issued within 14 days of purchase.",
    "Shipping is free for orders over 50 euros.",
    "Support is available on weekdays from 9 to 5.",
]
assert retrieve_top_k("Can I get my money back?", chunks, k=1) == [chunks[0]]
assert retrieve_top_k("When can I call for help?", chunks, k=1) == [chunks[2]]
top2 = retrieve_top_k("free delivery threshold", chunks, k=2)
assert len(top2) == 2 and top2[0] == chunks[1]
print("All retrieval tests passed!")

Build the evidence block with '\n'.join(...) over the retrieved chunk texts

practice_challenges.test_code:
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer, util

_model = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

def build_prompt(question, chunks, k=2):
    chunk_emb = _model.encode(chunks, convert_to_tensor=True)
    q_emb = _model.encode(question, convert_to_tensor=True)
    hits = util.semantic_search(q_emb, chunk_emb, top_k=k)[0]
    evidence = "\n".join(chunks[h["corpus_id"]] for h in hits)
    return (
        "Answer using ONLY the context below.\n\n"
        f"Context:\n{evidence}\n\nQuestion: {question}"
    )

chunks = [
    "Refunds are issued within 14 days of purchase.",
    "Shipping is free for orders over 50 euros.",
    "Support is available on weekdays from 9 to 5.",
]
prompt = build_prompt("Can I get my money back?", chunks, k=1)
assert "Context:" in prompt, "Prompt must contain a Context section"
assert chunks[0] in prompt, "The refund chunk must be retrieved as evidence"
assert chunks[1] not in prompt, "Unrelated shipping chunk must not appear with k=1"
assert "Question: Can I get my money back?" in prompt
print("All prompt assembly tests passed!")

q.en: Of the four RAG stages, which one costs real compute but is paid only once?
q.ta: RAG இன் நான்கு படிகளில், அதிக கணினி வளம் தேவைப்படும், ஆனால் ஒரே ஒருமுறை மட்டும் செய்யப்படும் படி எது?

en: Retrieving: ranking chunks for each question
Augmenting: pasting chunks into the prompt
Indexing: encoding every chunk into vectors
Chunking: splitting documents into pieces
ta: Retrieving: ஒவ்வொரு கேள்விக்கும் chunks ஐ வரிசைப்படுத்துதல்
Augmenting: chunks ஐ prompt இல் ஒட்டுதல்
Indexing: ஒவ்வொரு chunk ஐயும் vectors ஆக encode செய்தல்

q.en: Why split documents into 2-5 sentence chunks instead of embedding each whole document?
q.ta: ஒவ்வொரு முழு ஆவணத்தையும் embed செய்வதற்குப் பதிலாக, அவற்றை 2-5 வாக்கிய chunks ஆக ஏன் பிரிக்கிறோம்?

en: Chunking lets the LLM skip reading the context
The model can only encode one sentence at a time
Smaller chunks give vectors with fewer than 384 dimensions
One whole-doc vector averages topics and matches none well
ta: Chunking செய்தால் LLM context ஐப் படிக்கத் தேவையில்லை
மாடலால் ஒரு நேரத்தில் ஒரு வாக்கியத்தை மட்டுமே encode செய்ய முடியும்
சிறிய chunks இல் 384 ஐ விடக் குறைவான பரிமாணங்கள் கொண்ட vectors கிடைக்கும்
முழு ஆவணத்துக்கான ஒரே vector பல தலைப்புகளைச் சராசரியாக்குவதால், எதனுடனும் சரியாகப் பொருந்தாது
